label: 0051 · Smoothed in time, 1997–2025 (one QP over 53 windows): 0050 with fault meshes for the 2007 Chūetsu-oki, 2004 Chūetsu and 1995 Kobe earthquakes and afterslip for Chūetsu-oki and Kobe, uncorrelated noise, background coupling from −1 to 1, fourteen slow slip events as signal, fixed 747-site network, UNR positions (MAP)
description: 0050 with three new fault meshes. The 2007 Chūetsu-oki rupture is meshed on the Noto–Niigata block boundary, on its northwest-dipping plane (45° to 20 km): coupled, with free slip in its first year. The 2004 Chūetsu rupture is meshed along the Muikamachi fault zone (50° west-northwest to 20 km) for afterslip only: it lies inside a block, so it has no block-motion rate. The 1995 Kobe rupture is a vertical mesh on the block boundary from southern Awaji to Takatsuki, coupled in strike-slip; it can't carry the old segments' fault-normal shortening, which moves block motion in Kinki by about 0.7 mm/yr. Both Chūetsu earthquakes now start windows of their own (+91 and +365 days), so the base experiment has 53 windows and its station velocities differ slightly from 0050's in every window: cross-validation scores can't be compared with 0050's. The record has Omori afterslip for Chūetsu-oki (window cross-validation +85) and Kobe (+38). An afterslip state for Chūetsu 2004 scored −127 against free slip in each window of its first year, so it is left out and that mesh has free slip in its first year only. Chūetsu-oki afterslip reaches Mw 6.24 at 1 yr (the earthquake was Mw 6.62); near-field residuals in the first 24 days drop from 57 to 20 mm/yr. Kobe shows right-lateral slip of Mw 6.16 over 1997–2000, mostly deep beneath Kobe and the Rokko mountains, decaying to 0.2 mm/yr by 2025; coupling on the Kobe faults stays at 0.67–0.69 throughout. The network fit matches 0050's, slow slip Mw is within 0.03 and Kumamoto afterslip within 0.003.
